newsitem.title: USA: Democrat official says knew of no foreign tampering.
newsitem.headline: Democrat official says knew of no foreign tampering.

text.p: The finance director for the Democrats' 1996 fund-raising drive told a Senate investigation on Wednesday he never saw any evidence of a Chinese effort to influence the U.S. political process.

"None of the more sensational issues one hears mentioned from time to time ever materialised or came to my attention in the course of my work or the work of my staff in 1996," Richard Sullivan, former finance director for the Democratic National Committee, told the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee as it began hearing testimony on its second day.

He added: "That is I was never, I emphasise never, confronted at the time with any evidence or suggestion of wilful misconduct, foreign government influence, sell of office, contributions in violation of the Federal Election Campaign Act or other legal problems of that kind."

Committee chairman Sen. Fred Thompson, a Tennessee Republican, began the hearings on Tuesday describing what he called evidence of a plot by the Chinese government to influence the 1996 U.S. elections.
Sullivan said he was not a witness to any such effort.

"Nothing that I witnessed reflected adversely in any fashion on the diligence, good faith and hard work of anyone in a position of major responsibility assisting the president and the party with the 1996 presidential elections," he said.
